text.text_excerpt: Weeeeee hhhaaavvvveee aaa wiinnneerr!!! I am a 100% Thai food elitist. Having traveled through Thailand, I have had a lot of Thai food. Nothing in New Orleans has been able to fit the bill. Basil Leaf is terrible, Bangkok is so-so, Singha downtown is pretty good but never open. The place on Magazine is up and down. Singha Song is a beacon of light in the New Orleans well of Thai food. I had the two things I judge Thai places on: Green Curry and Tom Yum. The Tom Yum blew my mind. It was perfect, sweet, sour, with equal flavorings of lime, fish sauce and chili. I could live off of their Tom Yum. The Green Curry was perfect and served with some creative flair. I had leftovers. I think this is the best Thai food in town - its owned by the same people as Singha in downtown New Orleans. The service is fantastic and the decor is not too overbearing for a quiet dinner. I've never had lunch here, but its a favorite for a Friday night dinner with the family. They've been fighting with the neighborhood assocaition which doens't want any new liquor permits. The upside? BYOB with no corkage fee. The Pad Thai and Pad Woon Sen are delightful. The curry dishes are sharp, but not overwhelming. We LOVE their appetizers - fresh spring rolls, dumplings. I normally skip dessert, but you have to try the fried banana with ice cream. It's that good.

First perplexed thoughts upon unexpectedly running across Singha Song with no knowledge of it: "What? They're really going with that name? Wait, where are we? Did Chill Out Cafe redesign itself?" It's bizarrely positioned a whopping block from another long standing thai place-Chill Out Cafe. My impressions so far are positive, but I can't say it does anything special relative to its thai brethren. I've ordered the pad thai and the pad woon sen. Pad woon sen is my default thai dish because 1) I love it 2) it's a good way to compare restaurants based on the same dish. It was mostly as expected. Flavors were pretty on point.
